title: WordPress REST API Route Registration and Permission Callbacks
description: All custom WordPress REST API endpoints registered via register_rest_route() must declare an explicit permission_callback. Endpoints modifying state must verify authorization, nonces, or API tokens.
rules: Always define an explicit 'permission_callback' for every route.
Use '__return_true' ONLY for explicitly documented public read-only endpoints (e.g. public affiliate redirect resolution).
For authenticated endpoints, return a boolean or a WP_Error with a 401/403 HTTP status code from permission_callback.
Namespace all routes following the standard 'vendor/v{major}' convention (e.g. 'terso/v1').
anti_patterns: Omitting the 'permission_callback' argument (triggers PHP notices and severe security vulnerabilities in modern WordPress).
Using '__return_true' on POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE mutating endpoints.
Performing business logic or payload mutation inside the permission_callback function instead of the main callback.

patterns.name: Secure REST API Route Registration
patterns.description: Standard REST endpoint registration with permission callback and schema validation.

title: WordPress REST API Response and Error Standardization
description: REST API controller callbacks should return instances of WP_REST_Response for successful operations or WP_Error for failure conditions, ensuring consistent HTTP status codes and JSON payloads.
rules: Return new WP_REST_Response( $data, $status_code ) for all successful responses (200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content).
Return new WP_Error( $code, $message, array( 'status' => $http_status ) ) for business errors.
Wrap complex payload objects into arrays or DTOs before responding.
anti_patterns: Calling wp_send_json_success() or wp_die() directly inside a REST callback (bypasses REST Server formatting).
Returning plain PHP arrays without explicit HTTP status codes on creation/mutation requests.
Returning 200 OK with error payload strings instead of proper 4xx/5xx HTTP error codes.

patterns.name: Standard REST Controller Callback
patterns.description: Clean controller method returning WP_REST_Response and WP_Error.
